clue.text: Favour first of entrants in advance

parts.note: to favour something is to be for it, giving BE FOR

indicators.note: first of asks for the opening letter of the word entrants

explanation.surface: A judge gives preference to whoever entered first, ahead of the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Favour' reads as a noun but works as the verb phrase 'be for'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done earlier, ahead of time, happens previously, the adverb meaning of the answer.

clue.text: Sybil's husband in charge of church with ceremonial rights …

parts.note: Basil Fawlty, husband of Sybil in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers

explanation.surface: Basil Fawlty runs a church that enjoys special ceremonial privileges, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Fawlty Towers is a 1970s BBC sitcom about a hotel run by Basil and Sybil Fawlty. The definition takes in 'of church', which looks like part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a church granted special ceremonial privileges by the Pope; the adjective describes such a building.

clue.text: … fine means of securing congregation

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
a lock is a device that secures a door

explanation.surface: Continuing the church: a fine paid as a way of keeping the congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman's flock is the body of worshippers he looks after, a pastoral metaphor.

clue.text: Keeping hospital department in Orient running

indicators.note: in signals that the department sits inside the reworked letters of Orient
running suggests the letters of Orient are set in motion and rearranged

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital department is being kept open while running out in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orient' looks like the East, but 'running' scrambles it to RETION, which 'in' opens to hold the department.
explanation.definitionFit: Retention is the act of holding on to something, the noun sense of keeping.

clue.text: Eagerly grasps hurdle, having landed on bottom

parts.note: to hurdle is to jump over an obstacle
someone who landed on their bottom sat down

explanation.surface: A hurdler clears the barrier but ends up falling on their backside.
explanation.definitionFit: To leap at an opportunity is to seize it keenly, an idiom for accepting with enthusiasm.

clue.text: Trying case of drug popular in prison

indicators.note: in signals that the following pieces sit inside the word for prison

parts.note: jug is slang for prison

indicators.note: case of means the outer letters of the word drug, its shell

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A drugs trial in which someone popular sits in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' gives DG, which with IN goes into JUG.
explanation.definitionFit: Trying a case in court means hearing it and passing verdict, as a judge does.

clue.text: Doctor made one cut

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
to wed is to make two people one in marriage

explanation.surface: A surgeon performed a single incision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like an anagram signal for 'made', but it is MO.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass that has been mown has been cut with a mower.

clue.text: Killers axing third of villains they haven't met

indicators.note: axing means cutting a letter out of the word for killers

parts.note: stranglers are killers who throttle their victims

indicators.note: third of picks the third letter of villains

explanation.surface: Murderers wiping out one of their villainous partners whom they never knew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third of' villains is L, which 'axing' removes from STRANGLERS.
explanation.definitionFit: People who have never been introduced are unknown to each other, a fresh descriptive definition.

clue.text: What MP has turned up about good man's proclivities

indicators.note: about signals that the reversed word wraps around the saint
turned up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a Member of Parliament holds a seat in the House of Commons
ST, saint, is the crossword good man

explanation.surface: A politician's inclinations come to light around a virtuous person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reads a Commons seat upwards as TAES, and 'about' wraps it round the saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Proclivities are likings or preferences, which is what someone's tastes are.

clue.text: Unusually daring type of dressing

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of daring appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A bold, out-of-the-ordinary way to dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing clothes of the opposite sex, as a pantomime dame does, is a way of getting dressed.

clue.text: Hammer Thor needs taken up

indicators.note: to hammer something is to beat it out of shape, so the letters are bashed into a new order

explanation.surface: The Norse god's hammer needs lifting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammer' looks like Thor's weapon Mjolnir, but it is a verb signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Trousers taken up have been shortened at the hem, a tailoring sense.

clue.text: Arm first to back an argument

definitions.note: having words means having an argument, so the plural noun stands for a quarrel

indicators.note: first to back says the opening letter of the word for arm is moved to its end

parts.note: a sword is an arm, a weapon

explanation.surface: Arming yourself first to support a case in debate.
explanation.definitionFit: To have words with someone is an idiom for quarrelling with them.

clue.text: Compare Liberal with President Clinton, ultimately

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of President Eisenhower

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of Clinton

explanation.surface: Setting a Liberal politician beside Bill Clinton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'President' looks set to be Clinton, but it is Ike.
explanation.definitionFit: To liken one thing to another is to draw a comparison between them.

clue.text: Steps taken to bring about downfall?

definitions.text: Steps taken to bring about downfall?

parts.words: Steps taken to bring about downfall?
parts.note: the steps are dance steps and the downfall is rain falling, a ritual meant to summon showers

explanation.surface: Measures plotted to ruin someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'downfall' looks like ruin, but here it is precipitation, and 'steps' are dance moves.
explanation.definitionFit: A ritual performance meant to summon rainfall is made of dance steps to bring water down.

clue.text: Allocating roles in reconnaissance, keeping close to suspect

indicators.note: keeping signals the reconnaissance word holds a letter inside it

parts.note: casing a joint is a criminal's reconnaissance before a robbery

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of suspect

explanation.surface: Detectives assigning parts in a surveillance operation that keeps near a suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' gives T, which goes inside CASING.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre and film, deciding which actor plays which part is the director's selection process.

clue.text: Shielding light from poster in exhibition

indicators.note: in signals that the poster word sits within the exhibition word

parts.note: a showing is an exhibition or display
an ad, advertisement, can be a poster

explanation.surface: A poster in a gallery being protected from the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadow something is to cast shade over it, blocking the sun's rays.

clue.text: Assemble to conclude harvest

definitions.meaning: to assemble people is to bring them together
to harvest crops is to bring them in from the field

explanation.surface: Bring the farmhands together to finish the harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate definitions, with 'to' as link.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb can mean collect together, infer from evidence, or pick crops, covering all three senses.

clue.text: Serving up puff pastry cases closed restaurant

indicators.note: cases means the reversed letters enclose the word for closed
serving up in a down clue means the words are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a puff is a breath of air
a tart is a pastry
a door that is to is closed

explanation.surface: A restaurant serves puff pastry tarts before shutting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serving up' reverses AIRTART to TRATRIA, and 'cases' wraps it round TO.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian eating house, typically informal and family run, is a kind of restaurant.

clue.text: Westward retreat after conflict is admonished

indicators.note: after signals the reversed retreat comes after the conflict word

parts.note: war is conflict

indicators.note: westward in an across clue means read right to left

parts.note: a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: An army withdrawing to the west after fighting is told off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Westward' turns DEN into NED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reprimanded has been cautioned about their behaviour, a synonym.

clue.text: French man of letters charged and executed on retirement

indicators.note: retirement is withdrawal, going back, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: to charge is to tear along, past tense tore
executed means did, carried out

explanation.surface: A writer is indicted and put to death after retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' looks like put to death, but it means carried out.
explanation.definitionFit: Denis Diderot was the 18th-century French philosopher who edited the Encyclopédie.

clue.text: Dunno what victor does?

definitions.meaning: dunno is casual speech for I don't know
a winner defeats an opponent, so this is a victor's boast over the speaker

explanation.walkthrough: 'victor' looks like a name, but it is any winner.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a colloquial shrug meaning I have no idea, and literally describes a winner defeating the speaker.

clue.text: Girl to stop wearing underwear

indicators.note: wearing means the underwear word has the stop word on it, around it

parts.note: a bra is underwear
end means stop

explanation.surface: A girl has to stop wearing underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Brenda is a female first name, the crossword sense of girl.

clue.text: Limit flexible term accommodated by Devon banker

indicators.note: accommodated by means the following letters are housed within the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, a banker being something with banks

indicators.note: flexible says the letters of term can bend into a new order

explanation.surface: A Devon bank manager agrees a limit on flexible terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flexible' makes TREM from TERM. A 'banker' in crosswords is a river; the Exe flows through Exeter in Devon, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The extreme is the furthest point, the uttermost boundary of something.

clue.text: Narrowly avoids women's clothing

definitions.meaning: to skirt a problem is to edge round it, only just avoiding it
garments hanging from the waist worn by women

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both goes round the edge of and garments hanging from the waist.

clue.text: Characters from Kew longed to develop expertise

indicators.note: characters from says the letters of the following words are taken as raw material
to develop means those letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Botanists at Kew Gardens longing to build their expertise.
explanation.walkthrough: Kew is the Royal Botanic Gardens in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowledge is learning and understanding, much the same as expert skill.

clue.text: Article removed from shed very slowly

indicators.note: removed from means the article is taken out of the shed word

parts.note: a lean-to is a shed built against a wall
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Something has been taken out of the shed at a snail's pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a verb, but it is a garden building.
explanation.definitionFit: In musical directions, the Italian tempo marking means play at a slow pace.

clue.text: Tenor leading performers round Spain shut up in concert hall

indicators.note: leading means the tenor's letter goes in front
round signals that the performers word goes around the letter for Spain

parts.note: an act is a group of performers
E is the international vehicle registration for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A tenor heads a troupe touring Spain, trapped in a concert hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shut up' reads as locked in, but it is a command to be silent.
explanation.definitionFit: In a musical score the Latin marking tells a player to be silent, as an instruction in the concert hall.

clue.text: Take out royal household

definitions.meaning: to take someone out on dates is to woo them

explanation.definitionFit: The word means woo romantically, and the monarch's attendants and residence.

clue.text: Engaged in ceasefire, ignoring command

indicators.note: engaged in means the letters are held within the run of the following words

explanation.surface: Fighting during a truce, ignoring orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'command' looks like an order, but is the noun for rule.
explanation.definitionFit: To have command over a country is to rule it, the sovereign's period in power.

clue.text: Game's left-winger to make complaint

parts.note: a red is a socialist, a left-winger
to grouse is to grumble

explanation.surface: A sports fan with left-wing politics is set to complain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' is shot birds, and 'left-winger' looks like a footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: Game is wild animals hunted for sport, and this moorland bird is a prime example.

clue.text: Put one's hand to old hat to register departure

parts.note: to put one's hand to a document is to sign it
something old hat is out of fashion

explanation.surface: Touching an antique hat as a farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Recording one's leaving, as at a hotel or office desk, is done with a signature.

clue.text: Players leave evacuated fortress

parts.note: the cast is the set of players in a show

indicators.note: evacuated means the word leave is emptied, keeping only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Actors abandon a deserted stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle is a fortified stronghold, as built by medieval lords.
